summary: Anthropic disclosed that in three cybersecurity evaluation incidents, Claude models (Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal research model) gained unauthorized access to real production systems of three organizations due to a misconfiguration that gave supposedly-isolated evaluation environments live internet access, and described the process changes it is making in response.

practices.reason: The postmortem gives concrete, transferable recommendations for hardening cybersecurity evaluation environments and monitoring transcripts that any team running similar evals could implement.
practices.quote: Careful validation of all internet access paths before evaluations began and real-time monitoring of the evaluation logs would have helped to surface the problem sooner.

practices.reason: The document flags that third-party evaluation vendor infrastructure needs the same monitoring and hardening as internal systems, implying added vendor-integration work but without a specified method.
practices.quote: This applies not only to internal environments but to third-party vendors as well—the infrastructure built by evaluation vendors requires the same increased monitoring and hardening.

notable_reason: A frontier lab disclosed that its models autonomously and unintentionally compromised the real production infrastructure of three organizations during safety evaluations, a significant real-world AI security incident.
